items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-03
items.q: me and T-Bo, we got back together, you know. And we just made up a little band, you know, like that. Six-piece band, you know.

ctx.x: Come on, give me a right. What's it? Oh, me and T-Bo, we got back together, you know. And we just made up a little band, you know, like that. Six-piece band, you know. Who was with you? Who was with you? Well, Dr. Chani got five Chani come with us. We got Chani, you know. Eddie, Eddie, Eddie, and Eddie, Eddie, and Eddie, Eddie, and Eddie, Eddie, and Eddie, Jim Crow, you got his name? And we had him on Chani Bar. And we had Alcee, and myself, and T-Bo. Did I say Chani? Yeah. Yeah, Chani on drums then. Cornet?…
Ask him if this was before he was with Amos Riley or Amos Riley.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-03
items.q: We always worked together, me and T-Boy, you know. Bass and the bass stick together.

ctx.x: Who was the clarinet with Wesley Dimes? How was he? No, clarinet. Who was the clarinet player with Wesley Dimes?

Well, we just had one kind of player. So who was he? Who was the clarinet player? Oh, uh, Blind Freddy. Blind Freddy. Yeah. I see. Blind Freddy was a clarinet player at that time. Bass? T-boy. He called him Eddie Gilmore. He called him T-boy. He worked out by T-boy. Let's see. Now uh... Fetty Boo Boo. Yeah, Thumbo. You know, we called him Fetty Boo Boo, but he was...
We ain't no piano player then.
I think he's out in the country somewhere. Yeah?
I don't know, I see, he's got to have that team, he know where all those fellas are, you know. Yeah. And, uh, T-Boy, he was good. They talk about bass?
